sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-08-v16-quick/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 32; Internal Quality Checks row 32, no extra annotation)
evidence: Most of the 44 criteria are concrete, browser-observable outcomes with read-back evidence and distinctive probes (e.g. cw_save_reload_restart now re-reads two revisions and the first revision's source after restart_app; cw_restore_request_repeat_safe replays a recorded request and counts revisions in a fresh page; cw_preview_isolation uses rejecting fetch promises and a read-back localStorage value; visual likerts have anchors). The previously flagged undefined repeat handling is fixed: the Stop legs in cw_output_before_failure_kept (functional/judge.toml:254), cw_last_good_recovery (:290) and cw_stop_cancels_pending_work (:308) now define a void attempt, up to two repeats, and a fail when every attempt is void. But the new 'click Run, then click Stop straight away' in one code-runner action creates a different race the criteria do not handle: nothing tells the judge to confirm the run has actually started before Stop. The golden starts code asynchronously: PreviewRunner.run (solution/app/src/runtime.ts) only creates an iframe for /runner.html on the other loopback host. That page loads over HTTP, posts 'ready', gets the HTML through postMessage and runs it with document.write. stop() clears the token and removes the iframe at once. So a Stop that lands a few tens of milliseconds after Run can arrive before any user code has run. (1) In cw_output_before_failure_kept the Stop leg requires 'the marker written before the failure must still be visible', but if Stop beats the start, the marker is never written. The criterion then fails even for the golden or a conforming app, and the void rule only covers 'the timer had already fired'. This is a timing-dependent Oracle risk. (2) In cw_stop_cancels_pending_work (and the Stop leg of cw_last_good_recovery), the probe no longer shows that a timer, interval or Promise callback was pending when Stop was pressed, so it leaves no trace that the cancelled work ever existed. Also, in cw_output_before_failure_kept and cw_last_good_recovery the 4-second timer is given no observable effect, so the void condition 'if the timer had already fired before Stop' cannot be decided in the browser. Not measured: no raw-evidence index or full configured judge run exists for this candidate (the run dir holds only checklist/manifest/preflight), and I did not run the race, so how often the golden loses it is unmeasured.
counterexample: Conforming alternative that fails: the golden itself. The judge's code-runner does page.click(Run); page.click(Stop). If the runner.html iframe has not yet loaded, posted 'ready' and run the document.write'd script by the second click, stop() removes the frame before console.log(marker) runs. The console then lacks the Stop-leg marker and cw_output_before_failure_kept (weight 1.5) fails, with no void rule that applies. Plausible broken app that passes: an app whose Stop only discards a run still being prepared (for example it sets a flag checked before posting code to the iframe) and does nothing to timers, intervals or Promise callbacks once user code runs. Under the 'straight away' procedure Stop always lands in the preparation window, so the 4-second marker never appears and cw_stop_cancels_pending_work (weight 2.0) passes without Stop ever cancelling pending work.
suggested_fix: In all three Stop legs, have the draft print an immediate start marker to the console, and inside the same code-runner action click Run, wait (read-only, up to about 2 s) until that marker shows in the app console, then click Stop. Give the 4-second timer a visible marker, so 'void' means that marker appeared before Stop. In cw_output_before_failure_kept the start marker is the one that must survive.
